newsitem.title: CHINA: China reminds rival Taiwan of HK handover model.
newsitem.headline: China reminds rival Taiwan of HK handover model.

text.p: Beijing urged rival Taiwan on Sunday to regard the handover of Hong Kong as the model for its reunification with China, promising it greater prosperity under the communist flag.

The commentary issued by the official Xinhua news agency just hours before Taiwan is to begin two days of military exercises, apparently timed to proceed the July 1 handover of Hong Kong, showed no sign of Chinese anger at the war games.
"In just a few days, Hong Kong will return to China," said the commentary by Xinhua, mouthpiece of the government.

"This is a major step toward realising the reunification of the motherland under the 'one country, two systems' guide, and is extremely useful in setting an example for solving the Taiwan problem," it said.

The British colony of Hong Kong reverts to Chinese sovereignty at midnight on June 30 under the formula set out by late paramount leader Deng Xiaoping, which guarantees the territory's capitalist system will remain unchanged for 50 years.

Taiwan would enjoy even more autonomy than Hong Kong if it chose to reunify with China under the "one country, two systems" guidelines that Deng aimed initially to use to bring back Taiwan into the China fold, the Xinhua commentary said.
Beijing views Taiwan as a rebel-held province and says it will attack the island if it seeks independence.

Taiwan, still ruled by the Nationalists who were routed by communist mainland forces in 1949, espouses reunification -- but not until Beijing embraces a pluralist democracy that ends the communists' constitutional monopoly on power.

Deng's flexible formula would fulfil the desire of the people of Taiwan to be their own masters, while preventing separatists seeking independence for the island from splitting off an integral part of Chinese territory, the commentary said.
Taiwan has rejected Deng's formula, which would allow it to maintain its own army, saying it cannot reunify under the communist system.

"Through 'one country, two systems' to realise the peaceful reunification of the two sides of the Taiwan Strait, the people of Taiwan would not only not suffer any loss, but on the contrary they would gain from the strong support of the mainland," it said.
"(They) would and enjoy with the people of the motherland the same international respect and glory," it said.

China has tried to push Taiwan into diplomatic isolation as part of a campaign to force its Nationalist leaders to return to the fold, and has long regarded the return of Hong Kong as a strategic card in its campaign to persuade the Nationalists to reunify.

However, Beijing has avoided comment on Taiwan's decision to hold two days of military manoeuvres on Monday and Tuesday in a southern Taiwan district and in the Taiwan Strait just days before Hong Kong reverts to China.
China itself launched a series of live-fire games and missile drills in the narrow strait in March last year in a drive to intimidate the island before its first direct presidential elections.
Hong Kong newspapers have reported that China could respond with major "counterbalancing" manoeuvres.
The United States added its weight on June 11, warning both sides against staging exercises during the sensitive run-up to Hong Kong's handover.
